beats.act: the game, both clips, their routes
beats.narration_text: Walker Rudy is a 2D side-scroller in Godot four point seven, on the Compatibility renderer. This assignment adds two clips. Run, with its sword form, is the loop: a Sprite 2D whose frame an Animation Player keys, cut from a sheet of Rudy's own frames. Slash is the committing action: a cutout rig keyed as resource text, with startup, active and recovery. One Animation Player plays both, and only Rudy's state machine tells it what to play.

shot.observation: Two crops of the film's own Movie Maker capture of the real Main at 775c14c (play-01): Rudy running on cell 2 of the sheet, and Rudy mid-slash on the cutout rig; beside them the two clips, their routes, nodes, which loops and which commits, and the one authority.

beats.narration_text: The sheet first. This is the Sprite 2D under Look, in Rudy's scene. Its texture is the whole sheet: sixteen frames in one image. Two numbers slice it: h-frames four, v-frames four. That makes a grid of sixteen cells, numbered row by row from zero, and which cell is frame three is decided here, by the slicing, not by the picture. Scale one half, and the same offset every frame had, so his soles land on the origin in every cell.

beats.narration_text: Here is that sheet, with the grid drawn over it for the film. Sixteen cells of four hundred and ten by three hundred and eighty-six pixels: Rudy's sixteen Assignment 2 frames, packed by a script with no scaling and no edits, every cell checked against its source pixel for pixel. Run uses cells one and two, the sword run twelve and thirteen. On the right is what Godot actually drew from those cells: crops of the run preview, a fixture capture.

beats.act: the frame track that reads it
beats.narration_text: And this is the frame track that reads the sheet: the run clip. One value track on Sprite, colon, frame. Two keys: cell one at zero, cell two at point one two five seconds. Update one is discrete, so the frame jumps from cell to cell and never sweeps through the cells between. Length point two five, and loop mode one, linear. That is the seam rule for a frame track: no duplicate across the wrap. The last key is cell two, the first is cell one, and the gap from the last key to the end equals the key interval. Step, point one two five: one frame period, at eight cells a second.

beats.narration_text: The first question: what is a clip? This one, the slash's Grip track, is the whole answer. A track names a node path and a property: Slash Rig, Lean, Grip, colon, rotation degrees. Then keys: five times, five values, five transitions. Update zero is continuous, so the angle is interpolated between keys. Playing the clip means setting that property to those values at those times. Nothing in it knows about the sword, the goblin or the hitbox.

props.title: A Clip Is a List of Keys

beats.act: why a missing property fails silently
beats.narration_text: Why does a track that names a property that does not exist fail silently? Because a path is only text until the clip plays. A probe gave one clip a track to a missing node and one to a missing property. The missing node printed one warning, which the wrapper now fails on. The missing property printed nothing at all: that part simply does not move. So the read-back asks each node whether the property is in it. Mutation one dropped one letter, rotation degree. The game would load without a word; the read-back failed.

shot.observation: A card of recorded evidence: the load-error probe's track row and log line (evidence/load-error-probe/), test_rudy_clips.gd lines 419–421 verbatim, and mutation M1's diff and first FAIL line (logs/mutation_M1.txt). Labelled HEADLESS TEST OUTPUT.

beats.narration_text: The second question: what does one authority mean? Exactly one thing writes to an animated node. Here that is the Animation Player under Look. It alone keys the Sprite's frame and visibility, the rig's visibility, and Grip, Lean and the arc. Rudy's script writes only Look itself: its scale, for facing, and its alpha, for the flash, which no clip keys. And it tells the player what to play in one place, line two forty-one, every physics tick, restarting the slash on every new swing. With two writers on one node, the one that runs last in the frame wins, and that depends on node order, not on any design.

props.title: One Authority, One Call
props.source: Source: assignment-7/game/content/rudy/rudy.gd, lines 231–241 (verbatim). Godot editor reconstruction.
props.code:
_slash_clock = 0.0
		new_swing = true
		Sfx.play(&"slash")
	move_and_slide()

	_swing(delta)
	_count_down(delta)
	_look.scale.x = facing
	_look.modulate.a = 0.35 if is_invulnerable() and fmod(_invulnerable_left, flash_period) < flash_period / 2.0 else 1.0
	# Every new swing starts the slash clip over from its first key.
	_look.play_clip(_pick_clip(), new_swing)

He slashes while running: the selector switches to slash on the tick of the press, and back to the sword run on tick seventeen, starting over from cell twelve, and the rig is mirrored with him. The brief predicted what a second authority would look like: a flicker between a whole frame and a sheet cell. The read-back checks that no script sets the Sprite's texture or frame.

beats.narration_text: The third question: the two clocks. An Animation Player advances on the tick its callback mode names: the process tick, once per drawn frame, or the physics tick. Gameplay here reads on the physics tick: the hitbox is decided from the swing clock inside Rudy's physics process. So the player is set to physics, zero, here in the scene, not the default, idle. Both clocks are now the same tick. Its root node is Look, the parent, so every track path starts there. Autoplay is empty, so nothing plays a clip on its own, and speed scale is one.

props.title: Two Clocks, Made One

beats.act: result — one clock, in the strip
beats.narration_text: What one clock looks like, in the strip: a fixture, with the collision shapes drawn. Frame thirty, tick one: the wind-up, the hitbox dead. Frame thirty-one, tick three: the blade on its way, the hitbox live. Frame thirty-five, tick eleven, the first frame of recovery: blade forward, hitbox dead. The picture and the hitbox change on the same ticks. The state test checked it on every swing tick: the clip position equals the ticks since the press over sixty, and the largest disagreement is zero. On the idle callback, at thirty frames a second, the clip would have trailed by up to a drawn frame.

beats.narration_text: The fourth question: what it means to design feel in frames. The phase table is the design, in ticks at sixty a second. Startup, ticks zero and one, the hitbox dead. Active, two to ten, live. Recovery, eleven to sixteen, dead. On seventeen the swing ends. These are the game's existing timings, kept on purpose, though the motion reference's wind-up is fifteen times longer. The keys are derived from the table: zero, two, five, eleven and seventeen, over sixty. To change the feel, you change the table, and the keys follow.

props.title: The Phase Table, and the Keys Built From It
props.status: CHANGE-BRIEF.md §2.2 · the phase table, in ticks at 60 · beside the keys of rudy_animations.tres
props.source: Source: CHANGE-BRIEF.md §2.2 (296c6bdf) and Revision 6; game/animations/rudy_animations.tres lines 416–419. Drafted by Claude, reviewed by shuai-z.

beats.narration_text: The read-back writes the same table in ticks. Grip: tick zero, minus seventy; two, minus sixty; five, zero; eleven, forty-five; seventeen, fifteen; each with its transition. Lean, its position and the arc follow at the same boundary ticks. The test divides by sixty and compares each key time to within a microsecond, never with equals, because the file stores them as thirty-two-bit floats. And line one thirty-two is where tuning changed one number: the key at tick five eases out, point five, instead of in.

beats.act: result — the strip at each phase boundary
beats.narration_text: And the strip at each phase boundary. Movie Maker at thirty frames a second draws two ticks a frame, so two captures, a tick apart, cover every boundary. Startup into active: tick one, the blade back and the hitbox dead; tick two, the first active key, the hitbox live. Active into recovery: tick ten, the last live tick; tick eleven, the blade at forty-five and the hitbox dead. And the end: tick sixteen, the last slash frame; tick seventeen, the sword idle frame again. Each logged value matches the brief's table.

beats.act: tuning r1 — a reading, a change, a verdict
beats.narration_text: Then tuning. shuai-z watched the previews first, before Claude read a frame, and said: the three phases are distinct, and the sword does not catch as it sweeps. Claude's reading disagreed. From frame thirty-two to thirty-three the blade turns only five degrees, a near stop, because both keys around tick five eased in. That is a claim, and the record keeps both. One change, proposed by Claude and approved by shuai-z: the key at tick five eases out. Claude predicted Grip twenty-five on frame thirty-three and forty on thirty-four, and strip r one logged exactly those. shuai-z watched it in the game at a quarter speed, and kept it. That round was driven by Claude's reading, not by something shuai-z saw in play, so the observation-driven revision the assignment asks for is still owed.

beats.narration_text: The state machine is a priority list, run every physics tick. The mode decides first, in the lines just above these: celebrate, respawn, defeat, hurt. Then the swing: while the swing clock runs, slash. Then the air: rise, or fall, if he was moving sideways when the fall began. Then the floor: run if he is moving, idle if not. While he has the sword, the sword form of each. It returns a name, and the player plays it.

props.title: The State Machine Is a Priority List
props.source: Source: assignment-7/game/content/rudy/rudy.gd, lines 307–320 (verbatim). Godot editor reconstruction.
props.code:
return &"slash"
	var sword := gear == Gear.SWORD
	if not is_on_floor():
		var falling := velocity.y >= 0.0
		if falling and not _was_falling:
			_falls_sideways = absf(velocity.x) > 1.0
		_was_falling = falling
		if falling and _falls_sideways:
			return &"sword_fall" if sword else &"fall"
		return &"sword_rise" if sword else &"rise"
	_was_falling = false
	if absf(velocity.x) > 1.0:
		return &"sword_run" if sword else &"run"
	return &"sword_idle" if sword else &"idle"

beats.narration_text: What can end a committed swing early? Only the world: a hit, a fall out of the level, a respawn, the teleport circle. Here is the hit. Just above, with the sword, it knocks the sword away instead of a heart. He turns toward the hit. The swing clock goes below zero, so on that same tick the selector returns the hurt clip: the rig hides, the Sprite shows, and the hitbox is dead. Then the knockback.

props.title: What Ends a Committed Swing
props.source: Source: assignment-7/game/content/rudy/rudy.gd, lines 145–158 (verbatim). Godot editor reconstruction.
props.code:
Sfx.play(&"hurt")
	facing = -int(away) # he turns toward the hit
	_turn_time_left = 0.0
	_slash_clock = -1.0
	_invulnerable_left = invulnerable_time
	hit.emit()
	if not lost_gear and hearts <= 0:
		mode = Mode.DEFEATED
		velocity.x = 0.0
		defeated.emit()
	else:
		mode = Mode.HURT
		_hurt_time_left = hurt_time
		velocity = Vector2(away * knockback.x, -knockback.y)

beats.act: result — a hit in startup, active and recovery
beats.narration_text: Three takes, each a fresh boot of the game, scripted to time the slash against goblin B walking into his back. Take one: the hit on swing tick one, in startup. One drawn frame of the wind-up, then hurt, and the sword flies. Take two: tick five, mid-sweep, the hitbox live but on his other side. Hurt, on that tick. Take three: tick thirteen, in recovery. Hurt. In every phase the swing ends on the tick of the hit.

beats.narration_text: What the read-backs proved. One test reads both clips back against the player in Rudy's scene: fifty-one checks. Every track resolves to a real node and property. Key times match the phase table to a microsecond. The step is one frame period. Loop modes: linear for the run, none for the slash. Every frame track is discrete, and every frame key is inside the sheet. Thirty damaged copies each fail their own check. The state test, ninety-nine checks, drives the real game with key events and reaches fifty-four of the table's fifty-eight transitions; the other four cannot happen on Level one. The edge test presses before, on and after every phase boundary: a hundred and eight checks at sixty, sixty-six at thirty. And the pins pass again, with the three changes the brief predicted.

shot.observation: Recorded headless output through scripts/run-test.sh at pinned frame rates: the read-back's assertion lines and summary (51 PASS), the state test (99), the edge test (108 at 60, 66 at 30), the pin (20) and the earlier tests, read from logs/.

beats.narration_text: The four mutations, each in its own git worktree. One, a broken subname: exit one, six failures. Two, the run's loop mode set to none: exit one. Three, a frame keyed to cell sixteen, one past the sheet: exit one. Four, the import cache deleted and rebuilt: the read-back still passes, fifty-one, as predicted. The rig is keyed as resource text, not imported, so nothing the clips need lives in the cache.

shot.observation: Recorded output of the four mutations, each run in a fresh git worktree at f1680bfb (logs/mutation_M1–M4.txt): M1–M3 exit 1 with their FAIL lines; M4 exits 0 with 51 PASS after the cache was deleted and rebuilt; the control C0 passes.

beats.act: what no headless run can show
beats.narration_text: And what no headless run can show. Headless, Godot advances the clips and reads their structure, but it draws nothing: the probe asked for an image and got null. Whether the slash reads, whether the run wraps without a visible seam, whether the action feels committed: those rest on eyes. shuai-z's checks: the seam, no problem; play, no problem; registration and background, normal. Those words do not say how many wraps, which interrupts, or which stretches of the level.

shot.observation: The headless-facts probe's lines (logs/probe_headless_facts_60fps.log: clips advance; get_image() returns null), beside a fixture capture frame of the same slash; shuai-z's four human checks and editor run quoted from TEST-REPORT.md.

beats.narration_text: Verdict. Checked by machine: the read-back, the state and edge tests and the re-pinned pins pass, every earlier test keeps its count, and three mutations fail as they should; the fourth passes, as predicted. Checked by eye: shuai-z's first verdict, the kept round, four human checks and the editor run. Overruled: none of Claude's strip readings. On r zero the two disagreed, and Claude's reading drove the change. Caught by shuai-z: the brief's claim that every prompt reads the CLAUDE file, and Claude reading a rule from another file, measured frame counts, as this assignment's own. Caught by the tests and the sessions: a play-then-seek that ended the slash a tick early, a rig prompt that contradicted itself, previews one frame late, and two wrong citations in the brief.

beats.narration_text: Who made what. shuai-z chose both clips and their routes, kept the slash's timing, chose open footage and checked Claude's counts, approved every prompt, revision and commit, and gave every verdict and human check.
